entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon was a key figure in the Ghadar Party, a Sikh missionary and Indian freedom fighter who played a pivotal role in the planning of the 1915 Ghadar conspiracy in the British Indian Army.

Born in an unknown location with an unknown date, Dhillon's life was marked by his dedication to the Indian independence movement and his close association with prominent figures such as Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon and Subhas Chandra Bose.

Dhillon's significance extends beyond his involvement in the Ghadar conspiracy, as he also contributed to the revival of Sikhism during the British colonial era.

His legacy as a freedom fighter and missionary has endured, leaving a lasting impact on the Indian independence movement and the Sikh community.

'Empowering the downtrodden and fighting for freedom is the greatest duty of humanity.' - Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon
